findings.title: Ordering pause leaves customer checkout enabled
findings.why_it_matters: Customers can still enter checkout, complete the challenge, and press Place order while staff have paused online ordering; only the create request then returns a generic service error. The storefront derives `cafeOpen` solely from hours, while the public `CafeInfo` projection omits `ordering_enabled`, so the emergency capacity gate never reaches customer availability as U6 promises. Carrying the authoritative flag through the public café projection and combining it with hours restores the immediate pause behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an `orderingEnabled` field to `CafeInfo` and `getCafeInfo()`, derive checkout availability from both hours and that flag, and show a dedicated bilingual paused state before challenge/submission.
evidence: src/components/order/order-content.tsx:206-208 computes cafeOpen only from getOpenStatus(cafeInfo.hours), and lines 864-869 use only that value to gate submission.
src/lib/supabase/queries.ts:114-134 selects the cafe_info row but returns hours/contact/lead-time fields without data.ordering_enabled; src/lib/types.ts:96-108 has no field for the gate.
src/lib/orders/admin.server.ts:538-557 updates cafe_info.ordering_enabled, proving the staff control writes an authoritative value that the storefront projection drops.
docs/plans/2026-08-24-001-feat-order-lifecycle-hardening-plan.md:568 explicitly requires pausing to propagate immediately to storefront availability.

findings.title: Closing-time checkout offers impossible ASAP promise
findings.why_it_matters: During the final lead-time interval before closing, the page remains orderable and keeps ASAP available even though the authoritative RPC cannot promise pickup before close. For example, at 14:50 with a 15:00 close and 15-minute lead time, the customer completes checkout and verification only to receive `PICKUP_INVALID`. A checkout-specific availability calculation that includes lead time prevents advertising an option the server must reject.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute whether an ASAP promise fits before today's close using Montréal-local time and pickupLeadTime, disable ASAP/submission when it does not, and add a boundary test for the final lead-time interval.
evidence: src/components/order/order-content.tsx:95-119 applies pickupLeadTime only while building scheduled slots, while lines 206-208 treat every hours-open instant as checkout-open.
supabase/migrations/006_atomic_order_creation_expand.sql:389-417 adds pickup_lead_time to ASAP and mechanically rejects a promised time at or after close.
The base route only checked the current clock against hours for ASAP, so the new authoritative promise constraint makes this previously accepted UI path newly fail at the server boundary.

findings.title: Sample fixtures remain live ordering fallback
findings.why_it_matters: When an authoritative menu read fails, customers are shown fabricated products and prices that can now be added to the hardened cart, rather than an honest unavailable state. `fetchMenuItems()` still swallows configured Supabase failures and returns samples, while this diff changes sample item, modifier, and option identifiers into UUID-shaped values accepted by the client identity contract; a later create can only reject them as changed or unknown menu data. Restricting fixtures to explicit preview/development mode prevents a dependency failure from masquerading as a live café menu.
findings.suggested_fix: Permit sample fallbacks only behind an explicit preview/development marker; in configured environments propagate authoritative read failures to localized unavailable UI and disable ordering.
evidence: src/lib/data.ts:27-35 catches every configured Supabase menu error and returns sampleMenuItems; lines 38-46 similarly substitute sample hours/address/phone.
src/lib/sample-data.ts:257-283 newly assigns UUID-shaped item, modifier, and option identifiers, making fixture products satisfy the hardened client identity shape.
src/app/[locale]/menu/page.tsx:38-44 renders fetchMenuItems() directly into the live MenuContent, whose items are addable to the cart.

docs/plans/2026-08-24-001-feat-order-lifecycle-hardening-plan.md:65 forbids silently promoting sample menu, hours, price, address, or phone data to production authority and requires live ordering to fail honestly.

residual_risks: Hosted Supabase Auth/RLS/RPC/Realtime behavior, the real staging hostname and Turnstile edge, backup/key ownership, and U8 contract revocations remain intentionally unverified and owner-gated; the local proof must not be treated as launch authorization.

The local Turnstile proof uses the documented deterministic test credential plus a local Siteverify preload, so it cannot establish actual Cloudflare network, hostname, or widget behavior until the separately approved hosted canary.
testing_gaps: The real lifecycle Playwright tests sign staff into a second page in the same BrowserContext as the customer page, so the customer path inherits staff authentication; use isolated contexts to prove true guest checkout and tracking behavior.
No end-to-end test pauses ordering through the staff control, reloads the storefront, and asserts that challenge/submission are unavailable with bilingual pause recovery.
No boundary test covers the last pickupLeadTime minutes before closing, when the café is hours-open but no valid ASAP promise remains.
No configured-backend failure test proves that menu/content query errors render an unavailable state without sample products, prices, address, or phone.
